first_edition: William Lilly Christian Astrology (1647), Wellcome b30338724
title: If the Estate of the Native shall continue, or be Durable
scope: Historical hypotheses only; no independent human financial outcome, legality, or character claims.

source_groups.source_group: Printed CXVII header and principal source selection

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXVII If the Estate of the Native shall continue, or be Durable
claims.historical_only_meaning: Printed CXVII begins after a divider on the lower part of original PDF596; asks whether financial resources endure.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: principal Significators of Substance
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly bases endurance of estate on the principal wealth significators defined earlier, not solely the second-house cusp.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: he is ever that Planet who is posited in the second
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source initially prioritizes a planet physically in the second house for assessing durability.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if essentially dignified
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second-house planet's essential dignity is an explicit condition and cannot be ignored when selecting its signification.

source_groups.source_group: Benefic, strong and dignified second-house occupant means purported durability

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if this Planet be benevolent
claims.historical_only_meaning: A naturally or contextually benevolent second-house occupant is one component of the favorable case.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: powerfull
claims.historical_only_meaning: The occupant must also possess strength; the source does not treat planetary identity as sufficient.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: essentially qualified in dignities
claims.historical_only_meaning: Essential dignities are additionally required for the author's strongest wealth-persistence prediction.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: his Wealth will continue and remain without any disturbance
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly alleges continued resources without disruption under the compound favorable state; no financial observation is supplied.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: all his life time
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author describes an alleged lifelong property outcome rather than a one-year forecast, with no observation window.

source_groups.source_group: Weak second-house occupant: continuing income with loss episodes

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If that Planet be weak
claims.historical_only_meaning: When the selected second-house occupant is weak, Lilly gives a different mixed durability result.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: his Riches will continue, but with great hazard
claims.historical_only_meaning: Weakness is said to allow property to continue but with instability rather than automatically vanish.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: much difficulty to attaine ... great labour to preserve
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author alleges increased effort both to acquire and retain property under this natal condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: get good store of Wealth
claims.historical_only_meaning: Temporary accumulation of substantial wealth remains compatible with the negative/weak profile.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: suddenly again shall lose somewhat equivalent
claims.historical_only_meaning: Sudden losses roughly equal to gains are allowed despite continued overall wealth, making precise scoring difficult.

source_groups.source_group: Infortune in second house: strong/difficult versus weak/ruin

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If an Infortune be in the second
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly singles out a malefic occupying the second house, without declaring its mere presence categorically ruinous.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: consider if he be strong or weak
claims.historical_only_meaning: The dignity/strength of a second-house malefic decides between alternative outcomes.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if he be potent, the estate shall continue
claims.historical_only_meaning: A strong malefic is alleged to allow resources to persist, contradicting an unconditional negative Saturn/Mars rule.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: but with difficulty
claims.historical_only_meaning: In that strong-malefic branch, the continuation is explicitly qualified as difficult.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: subject rather to lose then lay up
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source predicts accumulation impediments even with resources persisting.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if he be unfortunate, his Fortune shall not continue
claims.historical_only_meaning: An unfortunate/debilitated malefic is assigned a contrary lack-of-continuation result.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: be overthrown and come to nothing
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly's maximal loss claim is described in absolute terms but has no external case proof.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: moderately fortified, frame your judgment accordingly
claims.historical_only_meaning: Intermediate dignities are assigned an unfixed intermediate outcome; the author gives no calibration.

source_groups.source_group: Multiple second-house planets and absence fallback

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If many Planets be in the second house
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source explicitly contemplates more than one occupying planet, requiring a prioritization rule.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: most powerfull
claims.historical_only_meaning: Among multiple second-house planets, the most powerful takes precedence rather than being averaged.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: according unto whose nature ... judge
claims.historical_only_meaning: The preferred planet's nature then conditions the durability judgment, a separate step after strength ranking.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If no Planet be in the second
claims.historical_only_meaning: An empty second house is an explicitly recognized common case rather than automatic missing evidence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the second house
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second-house ruler becomes a fallback significator when the second has no occupant.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Dispositor of Part of Fortune
claims.historical_only_meaning: The Part of Fortune dispositor is also named in the empty-second fallback, with ranking among the two not explicit.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: thereafter consider of Wealth or poverty
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author uses those fallback factors to resume general financial evaluation rather than assigning a blank chart.

source_groups.source_group: Directional timing: benefit promittors and estate significators

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: About what part of his life ... expect Wealth
claims.historical_only_meaning: The chapter separately asks when in the life course the gain could occur rather than merely if the estate continues.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators and Part of Fortune directed
claims.historical_only_meaning: Directions of wealth significators and Part of Fortune are offered as the preferred time calculation.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: to Beneficall Promittors
claims.historical_only_meaning: Favorable planetary promittors are stated targets of directions; their identity requires freezing in a real test.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: to Sextile Trine or [ambiguous symbol]
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source mentions apparently sextile, trine and one difficult-to-distinguish aspect marker in the timing string; preserve the glyph uncertainty rather than assert a precise algorithm.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the second
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second-house ruler is a listed timing target separate from any second-house occupant.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Dispositor of Part of Fortune
claims.historical_only_meaning: The dispositor of Part of Fortune is another possible directed contact, permitting multiple timing opportunities.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: or Planet in the second
claims.historical_only_meaning: Planets actually in the second house also supply possible targets, distinct from house ruler or Fortune dispositor.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: and their severall aspects
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly permits various aspects of these targets, with no stated fixed tolerance or penalty for multiple tests.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in what quarter of Heaven ... Significators
claims.historical_only_meaning: As a less exact general timing alternative, Lilly uses the house quadrant containing the strong wealth significators.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: especially him that is most fortified
claims.historical_only_meaning: The strongest significator is weighted preferentially for general life-stage timing.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: betwixt the ascendant and tenth house ... youth
claims.historical_only_meaning: If the relevant significators lie between the Ascendant and tenth house, Lilly alleges wealth increases during youth.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: ninth eighth or seventh ... Manhood
claims.historical_only_meaning: Placement in the ninth, eighth or seventh house is assigned a later life phase of wealth gain.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: full age ... twenty five to thirty five or forty
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second phase includes a broad author-defined age interval extending roughly 25 to 35 or 40.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: sixth fifth or fourth ... nearer old age
claims.historical_only_meaning: The sixth, fifth and fourth houses are assigned a further phase toward old age.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: after forty ... before fifty five
claims.historical_only_meaning: The older phase is described as after 40 but before 55, overlapping a preceding age band.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: third second or first ... latter end
claims.historical_only_meaning: The third, second and first houses are associated with the later part of the person's life.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: whether the Native ... live many or few yeers
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author says to adapt the life-phase timing to a prediction of the native's longevity, adding model flexibility.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: divide that time ... point out ... accesse to Riches
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly further permits subdividing the alleged lifespan to refine timing, but gives no independently calibrated method.

source_groups.source_group: Speed, orientation and direction concurrence modify timing

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Significators Orientall of the Sun ... time sooner
claims.historical_only_meaning: Wealth significators oriental to the Sun are alleged to accelerate the expected event time.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Occidentall ... nearer old age
claims.historical_only_meaning: Occidental significators are said to delay the outcome toward later age.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Retrograde Planets ... retard
claims.historical_only_meaning: Retrograde motion is separately said to postpone expected financial gains.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: direct and swift in motion ... hasten
claims.historical_only_meaning: Direct and swift motion is said to hasten events, a conditional alternative to retrograde delay.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: If Directions concurre with ... time limited
claims.historical_only_meaning: Concurrence between directional events and the earlier life-phase estimate is said to increase the interpreter's confidence.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: prove more certain ... confident
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly asserts increased reliability from agreement among his own calculations, but gives no blind evidence of calibration.

source_groups.source_group: Negative Saturn/Mars or other first-edition impediments

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Saturn Mars or [glyph unresolved] ... ill posited in the second
claims.historical_only_meaning: Poorly placed malefics or another source glyph in the second are alleged adverse; the last glyph must be independently verified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Lord of the second Combust
claims.historical_only_meaning: The second-house ruler combust is a further adverse condition, not an automatic conclusion from Saturn in the second.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Part of Fortune unfortunate
claims.historical_only_meaning: Affliction of Part of Fortune is separately named with the second-house ruler debility.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: confiscation of Estate banishment
claims.historical_only_meaning: The historical author asserts severe property/legal harms, but this is not evidence of criminality or actual legal outcomes.

source_groups.source_group: Luminary applications preserve or diminish inherited estate

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Luminaries applying to Planets in angles
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly gives a condition in which the Sun/Moon apply to planets occupying angular houses.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: continues in Estate ... left by Ancestors
claims.historical_only_meaning: Under angular applications the author alleges continuing roughly in the financial state inherited from one's ancestors.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: if they apply to Planets in cadent houses
claims.historical_only_meaning: Applications to planets in cadent houses form an opposite conditional case.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: diminisheth his Paternal stock
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author alleges reducing the paternal estate for cadent applications, not an objectively demonstrated outcome.

source_groups.source_group: Specific named fixed stars / points and Saturn morality claim

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Oculus Tauri, Cor Scorpionis, Caput Medusae
claims.historical_only_meaning: Three named fixed stars/asterisms are cited as allegedly harmful wealth indicators; the original glyphs and fixed-star ephemerides remain unverified.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: with Part of Fortune or joyned to his Lord
claims.historical_only_meaning: These stars/points must be in a specified relationship with Part of Fortune or its ruler; exact geometry is absent.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: loss of Riches ... threatens poverty
claims.historical_only_meaning: The historical text associates the fixed-star configuration with loss of estate and poverty, without actual event records.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: estate designed by Saturn ... covetous
claims.historical_only_meaning: Lilly asserts a covetous personality for Saturn-dominated estate sources; this stereotype is not a person-level character finding.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: when Sun and Moon have signification, then not so
claims.historical_only_meaning: The same stereotype is said not to hold under solar/lunar estate signification, showing another source-internal exception.

source_groups.source_group: Compound contrary-aspect and motion poverty forecast

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Infortunes behold the Significator of Substance
claims.historical_only_meaning: The source names hostile aspect(s) from malefics to a main estate significator as a prerequisite.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: both be Retrograde
claims.historical_only_meaning: Retrograde motion of both referents is an additional requirement whose exact plural antecedent needs review.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Cadent
claims.historical_only_meaning: Cadency is separately part of the adverse multi-factor condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Peregrine
claims.historical_only_meaning: Peregrine state is also present and cannot be silently equated with retrograde or cadent status.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: in Signes of contrary nature
claims.historical_only_meaning: Placement in opposed/contrary-nature signs further qualifies the complex negative condition.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Native will be perpetually poor
claims.historical_only_meaning: The author claims lifelong poverty under the compound configuration, without numeric wealth/age thresholds or any verified example.

source_groups.source_group: Following unnumbered third-house introduction and numbered brethren chapter navigation

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Judgments upon the third House Of Kinred, viz. Brethren and Sisters
claims.historical_only_meaning: An unnumbered third-house introduction begins after the decorative divider on source PDF598, distinct from the preceding wealth chapter.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: Nativity of the first borne
claims.historical_only_meaning: The following introductory paragraph recommends the oldest sibling's nativity for counting younger siblings; its substantive rules are not admitted in this wealth batch.

claims.anchor_not_diplomatic: CHAP CXVIII If have Brethren or Sisters
claims.historical_only_meaning: The next printed numbered chapter opens lower on original PDF598, following the unnumbered third-house introduction, and continues into PDF599.
